speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; to help you, please describe exactly where the pain is located, what triggered it, and if you notice any swelling, redness, or deformity.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis (with possible secondary Carpal Tunnel Syndrome given the radiation to the elbow). The history of a fall six months ago suggests a fracture non-union or post-traumatic osteoarthritis, but the specific location (thumb/wrist), aggravation by holding an infant (adduction of thumb), and relief with ice strongly point towards overuse tenosynovitis.

REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Hand_Ultrasound or Right_Hand_Xray
